output.review_comment:
Approving. The change uses general title-case rules and doesn't hardcode any test inputs. No test files are touched, as the teammate asked. I only had the diff, so I couldn't run the suite myself; confirm CI is green before merging.

What changes:
1. Words with an uppercase letter after the first character (e.g. "iPhone", "NASA") are kept as-is.
2. Small words stay lowercase except as the first word, the last word, or the word right after a colon (the start of a subtitle).
3. All other words are capitalized.

These are standard editorial rules, and the old code was missing the last-word and after-colon exceptions.

Non-blocking suggestions:
- Rule 1 runs before the small-word check, so an all-caps small word like "AND" or "OF" stays uppercase. That's probably fine for acronyms, but confirm it's what the editorial team wants.
- Punctuation at the start of a word isn't handled. `'"the'.capitalize()` returns `'"the'`, so a quoted first word stays lowercase. The same applies to the existing capitalize path.
- The subtitle check looks at `result[-1]`, the previous word after it has been processed. That works, but checking `words[index-1]` would be simpler. Also, `.rstrip()` does nothing there, because splitting on spaces leaves no whitespace to strip.
- There's no PR description. Please add a short summary of the rules being implemented.
